note: Single source for the human-need vocabulary (D27 Concept, W-66). The intent-slot schema enum, the system prompts, the ontology entity human_need_concept, the Java bundled schema and the grading screen must all list exactly these ids; test_vocabulary.py and the Java tests fail if any of them drifts. Definitions, aliases and asks are proposals awaiting Nate's review (Q-OC-11). Asks are deliberately empty where nobody has reviewed a mapping: a need never picks a device by itself.

decided.cold, hot, stuffy, dark, arriving, leavi: Seed set from D27 (Cowork, 2026-10-14); awaiting Nate (Q-OC-11).
decided.light, nap, wake_up: Added by Nate, 2026-10-16, while grading gold-01: the vocabulary had dark but not the want for light, and bedtime but not nap or wake up. 'bright' is a synonym of light, recorded as an alias so one idea has one label.

concepts.label: Stuffy
concepts.definition: The air feels stale or close. Not a temperature complaint, so never a temperature threshold.

concepts.label: Dark
concepts.definition: States that it is too dark: a lack of light described as a condition ("it's dark in here", "I can't see"). Wanting light or brightness as the thing asked for is `light`.

relates_to.note: Wording decides: a stated lack is dark, a stated want is light. Both are satisfied by adding light.

concepts.label: Light
concepts.definition: Wants light or more brightness, stated as the thing wanted ("I need more light", "it needs to be brighter"). 'Bright' and 'brighter' mean the same and are aliases, not a second concept. The opposite wish (too bright, want less light) is not in the vocabulary yet.

relates_to.note: Wording decides: a stated want is light, a stated lack is dark.

examples: It needs to be brighter in here

concepts.label: Arriving
concepts.definition: The person is arriving, or about to arrive, at the place.
examples: I am on my way in

concepts.label: Leaving
concepts.definition: The person is leaving, or about to leave, the place.

concepts.label: Bedtime
concepts.definition: Going to bed for the night.

relates_to.note: A nap is a short daytime rest.

concepts.label: Nap
concepts.definition: A short rest during the day, not going to bed for the night.

relates_to.note: Bedtime is sleeping for the night.

examples: I'm going to take a nap
I need to lie down for a bit

concepts.label: Wake up
concepts.definition: Waking up or getting up now. A request to be woken at a future time ("wake me at 7") is a schedule, not this need.

concepts.label: TV time
concepts.definition: The person wants to watch television.
